newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Comalco expects to sell wheel plant to U.S. group.
newsitem.headline: Comalco expects to sell wheel plant to U.S. group.

text.p: Australian alumunium producer Comalco Ltd on Tuesday said it expected to soon sell its aluminium wheel manufacturing plant in the island state of Tasmania to U.S. metals group, Reynolds Metals Co.
Comalco spokesman Ian Head declined to disclose the sale price or the book value of the asset but said the impact on Comalco's profit and loss account would not be material.
But he confirmed a newspaper report that the company had invested around A$50 million (US$38 million) in the plant, which makes wheels for domestic and overseas car manufacturers.
"We have been discussing it with them for several months and we would expect to reach agreement within the next few weeks," Head told Reuters.
The final sale agreement is pending the resolution of legal issues, he said. "There are some legal formalities," he added.
The sale will complete Comalco's programme of selling aluminium fabricating assets and focusing on its mining, refining and smelting businesses.
"This wheel plant is the last of the downstream operations and when it's sold, that will represent our withdrawal from downstream activities," Head said.
"This has no impact on our commitment to smelting. We remain fully committed to our smelting plants," he added.
